subject.title: Add Herdr state bridge for OpenClaw TUI

question: Should Herdr pane-state reporting be accepted as a bundled OpenClaw plugin-gated TUI integration, explicit core-owned TUI behavior, or kept outside core for ClawHub/Herdr-owned packaging?
rationale: The PR is a useful optional integration, but it adds an ambient env-triggered runtime loop and a default-on bundled plugin shape, so the permanent owner boundary must be chosen before merge.

options.title: Bundle Behind Plugin Policy
options.body: Accept the integration only if startup honors resolved plugin enablement, allowlist, denylist, and per-plugin disablement, with live Herdr proof before merge.

options.title: Own As Core TUI Behavior
options.body: Treat `HERDR_PANE_ID` as an explicit core TUI feature, remove the misleading no-op plugin wrapper, and document the env-triggered runtime surface directly.

options.title: Move Outside Core
options.body: Pause or close the PR unless a missing OpenClaw TUI/plugin API is proven, and route the integration to ClawHub or Herdr-owned packaging.

recommendation.title: Bundle Behind Plugin Policy
recommendation.body: Accept the integration only if startup honors resolved plugin enablement, allowlist, denylist, and per-plugin disablement, with live Herdr proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans plugin policy, TUI lifecycle, and whether optional integrations belong in core, all areas reflected in recent history.
